c.tagline: Russia's Pacific gateway — end of the Trans-Siberian, city of bays, bridges and seafood.

taxi.fareNote: Most rides are booked through apps like Yandex Go and Maxim; street hailing is uncommon.

emergency.note: 112 is Russia's unified emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Watch for petty theft and drunken confrontations around late-night bars near the station and Sportivnaya Harbor.

hood_desc: The downtown grid around Aleutskaya and Svetlanskaya streets, anchored by the Trans-Siberian Railway's eastern-terminus station, the GUM department store and views up to the Golden Bridge — the walkable base for first-timers.
Sportivnaya Bay and its seaside promenade: the city beach, the ferris wheel, arcades, seafood cafes and bars — Vladivostok's liveliest strolling and nightlife strip.
A hilly peninsula reaching south to the Tokarevsky (Egersheld) lighthouse on its sandspit, with panoramic sea views and quiet older streets away from the bustle.
The steep hillside around the funicular and the Eagle's Nest (Orlinoye Gnezdo) viewpoint — the classic panorama over the harbour and Golden Bridge, marked by the Cyril and Methodius monument.
The Amur Bay waterfront northwest of center, lined with embankments, sanatoriums and summer swimming spots; a calmer, greener residential stretch.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; tap water quality is unreliable.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; the funicular operates about 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
transit.note: Vladivostok relies mainly on an extensive city bus network across its hilly peninsula, plus a short historic funicular climbing Eagle's Nest hill; there is no metro.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash or tap a contactless bank card on board; fares are a flat low rate per ride.

ferry: Local passenger ferries across the Golden Horn Bay and to Russky Island and nearby islands
train: Trans-Siberian Railway eastern terminus (Vladivostok station) to Khabarovsk, Moscow and beyond
Airport rail link to Knevichi (Aeroexpress-style, reduced service)

transit.m: Airport express train / bus №107 to Vladivostok railway station (~50-90 min)
Taxi or Yandex Go to city center (45-60 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; leaving around 10% for good restaurant service is common in nicer places.

food.name: Kamchatka king crab
food.desc: Giant Far Eastern crab, usually steamed and served by the leg or in phalanges with butter; the single dish Russians fly to Vladivostok for.

places.name: Zuma
places.note: The city's best-known Pan-Asian seafood restaurant; live crab tanks and a huge shellfish list.

places.name: Fantome
places.note: Crab picked live from the aquarium and cooked to order alongside daily-landed shellfish.

places.name: Vinovatye Zvezdy
places.note: Praised for king crab at fair prices, plus a seasonal taiga-inspired menu.

food.name: Far East scallops
food.desc: Sweet Yesso scallops from Peter the Great Bay, eaten raw with lime, grilled in the shell or baked with cheese and garlic butter.

places.name: Zuma
places.note: Scallops raw, seared and baked; the reference kitchen for Primorye shellfish.

places.name: Vinovatye Zvezdy
places.note: Raw scallops and oysters plus marinated salmon in a candlelit dining room.

places.name: Ogonek Grill and Bar
places.note: Open-fire grill that does scallops and other local seafood over coals.

food.name: Pyanse
food.desc: Vladivostok's street-food icon: a fist-sized steamed bun of cabbage and minced meat, borrowed from Korean pigodi and sold from kiosks citywide.

places.name: Pyan-Se kiosks
places.note: The original chain of green kiosks; buy them hot from the steamer for pocket money.

places.name: Sportivnaya Market food row
places.note: Korean stalls in and around the market steam pyanse all day next to the kimchi sellers.

places.name: Millionka
places.note: Old Chinatown-themed restaurant serving sit-down versions of the city's Asian street classics.

food.name: Kuksi
food.desc: Chilled Korean-Russian noodle soup in icy beef or vegetable broth with cucumber, egg and chilli, a Vladivostok summer staple since the Soviet era.

places.name: Sportivnaya Market food row
places.note: Korean vendors ladle kuksi from steel vats; the most authentic and cheapest bowls in town.

places.name: Millionka
places.note: Restaurant version of kuksi and other Korean-Chinese dishes in a historic quarter setting.

places.name: Nostalgia Cafe
places.note: Long-established cafe by the funicular mixing Russian and local Asian-influenced dishes.

food.name: Trepang with honey
food.desc: Far Eastern sea cucumber, prized as a tonic, sliced and served in honey or as a cold salad with garlic and soy.

places.name: Zuma
places.note: Reliable place to try trepang prepared several ways, including the classic honey cure.

places.name: Fantome
places.note: Fresh shellfish counter that regularly carries trepang alongside urchin and crab.

places.name: Sportivnaya Market
places.note: Seafood rows sell jarred trepang in honey to take home; ask for the local Primorye catch.

food.name: Spot prawns and sea urchin
food.desc: Sweet red botan shrimp eaten raw or lightly steamed, and spoonfuls of orange urchin roe straight from the shell with lemon.

places.name: Zuma
places.note: Deep raw bar with shrimp, urchin and oysters from Peter the Great Bay.

places.name: Vinovatye Zvezdy
places.note: Small seafood-led menu that changes with the daily landings.

places.name: Sportivnaya Market
places.note: Fish rows where locals buy live shrimp and urchin; some stalls will shuck on the spot.

food.name: Taiga herbal tea
food.desc: Infusion of Primorye forest plants such as schisandra berry, chaga and eleuthero, served hot with honey. Non-alcoholic and widely poured after meals.

places.name: Vinovatye Zvezdy
places.note: Runs a taiga-themed menu, including forest teas and infusions from the region.

places.name: Nostalgia Cafe
places.note: Samovar-style teas plus jars of local honey and berry preserves to go with them.

places.name: Sportivnaya Market
places.note: Stalls sell dried schisandra, chaga and pine-nut mixes to brew yourself.

food.name: Primorye craft beer
food.desc: Vladivostok has one of Russia's liveliest craft scenes, with local breweries pouring pilsners and IPAs, plus the old Soviet-era Vladivostok lager.

places.name: Ogonek Grill and Bar
places.note: Grill bar with local drafts, a favourite pre- or post-dinner stop downtown.

places.name: Millionka
places.note: Atmospheric bar-restaurant in the old Chinese quarter with regional beers on tap.

places.name: Admiral Fokin pedestrian street bars
places.note: The city's bar strip; several taprooms pour Primorye-brewed beer near the waterfront.

landmarks: Golden Bridge (Zolotoy Bridge)
The soaring cable-stayed bridge across Golden Horn Bay, built for the 2012 APEC summit, instantly became Vladivostok's defining modern symbol.
Russky Bridge
The world's longest cable-stayed span leaps 1,104 metres to Russky Island, its colossal pylons dwarfing the strait it crosses.
Eagle's Nest Hill and Funicular
Ride the city's beloved Soviet-era funicular toward this summit viewpoint, where the panorama of bridges, bays and hills is pure Vladivostok.
Vladivostok Railway Station
The ornate terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway, where a platform pillar marks kilometre 9,288 from Moscow at the line's Pacific end.
Tokarevsky Lighthouse
A slender white lighthouse from 1876 at the tip of a narrow causeway, reachable on foot at low tide with sea views toward Russky Island.
S-56 Submarine Memorial Museum
A decorated WWII submarine beached on the waterfront, its cramped compartments and torpedo room preserved alongside the Pacific Fleet's memorial flame.
Voroshilov Battery (Vladivostok Fortress)
Massive twin battleship-gun turrets hidden on Russky Island, the dramatic highlight of the tsarist-era fortress system ringing the city.
Primorsky Aquarium (Oceanarium)
One of the world's largest aquariums, a futuristic shell-shaped complex on Russky Island showcasing Pacific marine life from belugas to tropical reefs.
Sportivnaya Harbour and Admiral Fokin Street
The city's seaside promenade and its fountain-lined 'Arbat', where locals stroll from pebble beach sunsets into buzzing café-filled evenings.
Triumphal Arch of Tsarevich Nicholas
A jewel-box brick-and-tile arch rebuilt to honour the future Nicholas II's 1891 visit, standing colourfully above the Golden Horn waterfront.

train.note: Vladivostok is the eastern terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway, and the Rossiya train to Moscow takes about six days across seven time zones - the classic journey, booked months ahead in summer. The through carriages to Harbin and Beijing in China and the link to Tumangang in North Korea have not run reliably in recent years, so treat the international services as unavailable. Foreign cards often fail on the RZD site.

intl.op: regional Russian and Chinese coach operators — tickets at the Vladivostok bus station, no online booking

bus.note: Cross-border coaches run east to the Chinese border towns of Hunchun and Suifenhe, taking five to eight hours including a slow border check - you need a Chinese visa arranged in advance. Domestic buses from the central bus station serve Ussuriysk, Nakhodka and Khabarovsk. Check current border-crossing status before relying on the China services.

intl.op: DBS Cruise Ferry / Eastern Dream — tickets through Vladivostok agents, service status varies

ferry.note: Vladivostok's international ferry to Korea and Japan has operated on and off in recent years and its status has been unreliable since 2022 - confirm directly before planning around it. When running, the Eastern Dream sails roughly weekly from the Marine Terminal beside the railway station, taking about 20 hours to Donghae and longer to Sakaiminato. Local boats cross the bay to Russky Island and the Popov islands in summer.

full.name: Ussuriysky Nature Reserve
full.blurb: Ussuriysky Nature Reserve protects old-growth Amur River basin forest with hiking trails, roughly two hours north of Vladivostok.

full.name: Nakhodka
full.blurb: Nakhodka is a port city east of Vladivostok on the Sea of Japan, with rocky beaches and a working harbor.
